blocking_findings.evidence: execution/fetch_ir_documents.py process_ticker records exc.committed counts but never adds the URL to `already`. On the next run the DB row's source_url places the URL in `already`, so only the skip path runs. That path calls src/pipeline/managed_ir_sources.py replay_registered_issuer_document_publications -> _replay_registered_result. _replay_registered_result first reads data/managed_ir_publications/<attempt>/publication_result.json. When _finalize_committed raised publication_committed_partial before the result was written (inventory_state failed or result_state not_started), that file does not exist. read_stable_artifact then raises OSError, which becomes 'registered_publication_result_invalid', and the run reports projection_failed/failed. Every later run repeats this, so the publication stays permanently failed. publish_prepared_issuer_documents can finalize from the durable managed_ir_publications row plus the retained attempt staging receipt, but no caller reaches it once the URL is registered. The existing test (test_missing_committed_result_blocks_projection_repair_without_source_work) deletes the result file after a full success; it does not exercise a real finalize failure.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: When the result artifact is absent, have replay_registered_issuer_document_publications load the request from the attempt's staging_receipt.json, verify it against managed_ir_publications.staging_receipt_sha256, and call publish_prepared_issuer_documents to finalize. Add a test that injects a failure in _finalize_committed (inventory and result phases), reruns automatic and manual intake, and asserts finalization, projection, anchor/dirty effects and no new download or classification.
blocking_findings.title: Committed-but-unfinalized managed publication can never be recovered

blocking_findings.evidence: process_ticker now replays every already-registered URL on every categorize run, not only when the index alias needs repair. The replay goes through publish_prepared_issuer_documents -> _read_completed_receipt, which requires classifier_code_identity() and verifier_code_identity() to equal the sealed values and re-runs _policy at today's date. classifier_code_identity hashes execution/fetch_ir_documents.py and about ten other files; verifier_code_identity hashes managed_ir_sources.py, sqlite_runtime.py, job_runtime.py and others. This candidate itself edits fetch_ir_documents.py and managed_ir_sources.py. After any such edit, every committed managed presentation whose URL remains in a manifest raises staging_code_identity_changed. The skip path then increments projection_failed and failed and `continue`s before ready_existing, which produces: status failed, fetch CLI exit 1, discovery _fail (no anchor when ready_work==0), and register_urls returning 0 with ir_fetch_status 'failed'. All of this happens even though the DB row, canonical file and index alias are correct. The cost also grows quadratically: each URL replays every same-quarter publication. The evidence note treats old-receipt requalification as a deployment obligation, but this candidate makes it a recurring breakage on every code edit.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: On the skip path, first check the compatibility alias against the registered documents row using a cheap read. Replay or repair only when the alias is absent or invalid. Report code-identity drift on an already-coherent registration as a distinct non-failing requalification_required outcome, not as projection_failed. Add a test that changes the identity (monkeypatch) after a successful publication and asserts that the CLI, discovery and manual adapters still succeed with no network or classifier work.
blocking_findings.title: Routine skip path turns code-identity or policy drift into permanent caller failure for coherent registrations

blocking_findings.evidence: src/index_manager.py project_ir_document (newly_published=None) returns False only when the incumbent equals one of the managed candidates. Any other incumbent, including a valid alias for a different document at the same quarter/type key (a later categorizer/user-intake or legacy registration), falls through to register_ir_document with processed=False when there is one candidate. This contradicts the docstring 'repair only an unambiguous missing alias' and the evidence claim that only a missing or invalid entry is repaired. The 'invalid_entry' test covers only an entry missing required fields. Concretely, a routine fetch run can silently replace the owner's later-selected presentation alias and clear its completion flag. That flag is narrative-completion authority that R3 explicitly kept.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: Write only when the key is absent or the incumbent lacks the required projection fields or fails its schema. If the incumbent is a well-formed alias for a different document, preserve it and report a non-destructive 'alias_held_by_other_document' outcome. Add a test with a valid foreign incumbent.

blocking_findings.evidence: execution/fetch_ir_documents.py process_ticker: `_download` returning None (404, HTML-not-document, transport failure) increments `failed`. The status becomes 'failed'/'partial' and `_exit_code` returns 1. The baseline always returned status 'done' with exit 0, and the module docstring still says transport failures are 'logged and skipped'. In execution/discover_ir_documents_all.py `_finish_discovery`, `fetch_failed and not ready_work` returns `_fail(...)` before the process block. This happens even when `discovery.processing_pending` or `has_pending_narrative` is true. A single persistent dead or HTML link in the recent manifest window, which is common in crawler manifests, therefore marks the ticker FAILED on every run. It also permanently suppresses deterministic anchor/brief_dirty processing of previously registered documents. That is a regression in progressive research. register_urls likewise returns 0 (exit 1) if any one URL fails.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: Report download/no-document failures separately from post-download registration, publication and projection failures (for example a `transport_skipped` count). Keep exit 0 and status non-failed for transport-only skips. In `_finish_discovery`, still run the process stage when pending work exists even if the fetch failed, and report failure separately from processing. Add tests: one dead link alongside existing registrations, and pending narrative work with a failed fetch.
blocking_findings.title: R2 turns best-effort transport skips into hard failures, and discovery then skips pending narrative processing

blocking_findings.evidence: src/pipeline/managed_ir_sources.py: `_durable_recovery` and `_read_inventory_evidence` compare the stored binding to `_publication_binding(root, db_path)`, which includes `str(_code_root())`. `replay_registered_issuer_document_publications` now runs this replay for every already-registered managed presentation URL on every fetch, manual and discovery run, through `_replay_registered_result` and `_replay_result`. The baseline skipped registered URLs. Two cases trigger the failure: a publication made from a different checkout (for example a codex worktree versus /Applications), or a configured-DB mismatch in `_configured`. Either one raises `publication_record_mismatch` or `configured_database_mismatch`. fetch_ir_documents then records `projection_failed`/`failed`, so the run fails permanently for that ticker. The test for drift only varies `classifier_code_identity` and `_policy`, never the code root.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: For read-only historical inspection, validate the record against its own sealed binding plus state root, database and canonical bytes. Do not compare it to the current code root. Surface a binding difference as `requalification_required`. Add a test that publishes under one code root and replays under another.

CategorizationFailure, ticker mismatch or low confidence fail in managed staging before reaching the legacy categorizer's handling. Legacy families therefore do not fully 'retain supported routes'. Legacy files are also classified twice and leave a retained staging copy.
Removing the broad `--source-dir ir_documents` sweep may strand local uploads that relied on fetch's incidental sweep. No evidence shows a scheduled route that covers them.

The in-process `_run_categorize` catches only OSError, ValueError, ImmutableArtifactConflictError, SecureFileInstallError and sqlite3.Error. Other exceptions abort process_ticker without summary JSON. `IR_PROJECT_ROOT` is no longer set, and only some `process_ir_document` index calls received `document_index_path`.

`_historical_receipt` raises with `committed=True` even on the fresh-publication path. The `replay_registered_*` docstring says 'without writer locks', but incomplete finalization calls the locked publisher.
Every run now re-hashes the canonical PDFs of all registered managed presentations. This runtime cost is unmeasured.
units.scope: Calendar-year PDF ir_presentation managed registration, automatic and manual callers, explicit recovery outcomes

findings: Real deletion: all three callers (discover, onboard, refresh_dispatch) invoke the real CLI with explicit --repo-root/--db. Module-global, path and sys.argv rebinding are gone. Cache, index, event and regenerate-missing selectors are tested against an explicit state root, including `--all` and dry-run behavior.

The prior adapter called `db.set_db_path(db, state_root=state_root)` process-wide. The replacement scopes only `db_path_context(db_path)` around anchor and LLM calls, and drops the state_root binding. The tests stub `generate_*`/`load_*` and check only `resolve_db_path(None)`. Nothing shows that real llm_client internals (usage/budget/cache) resolve through the context rather than `db.DB_PATH` or a state-root binding.
Legacy completion flags and cache existence remain completion authority, as scoped.
units.scope: Explicit-state adapter retirement only (process_ir_documents_state.py deleted; completion authority not migrated)

findings: Traced: the numeric projection matches the old parser, including duplicate-period column overwrite, later same-name config overwrite only on non-empty series, `max_quarters` window, bool exclusion, rejected-row fallback with no series, and configured-name order. `parse_spreadsheet` is now a projection.

Winning-record provenance: the winner cell's locator, header, raw label, scale and raw value reach the writer through `selected_series`. Bytes and config are re-hashed before writes. Run-dedupe identity matches the numeric path (the test asserts suppression).

The only semantic delta is the `metric_name_as_reported` raw-label enrichment. Lane, status, basis and period are unchanged and use the same `unclassified_kpi_context` factory. Unsupported cells are explicit skips.
Synthetic cost: about +3% parse time. Durable rejected-cell capture is correctly not claimed.
units.scope: Source-preserving spreadsheet parser to existing KPI writer handoff (native writer not retired)

findings: Real retirement: `_BatchFactReadModel`, the duplicated batch savepoint guard and the scalar bundle rereads are gone. Paired synthetic output equality was reported with large select and verifier reductions; DCF shows parity.

Snapshot ownership: traced `publication_verification_scope`. Nested same-connection reuse holds. Commit+rebegin is detected at RELEASE, and the scope neither rolls back a replaced transaction nor drops the replacement write. A transaction the scope did not create is never rolled back. Row factory is restored.

Clocks: selection uses K/O, while bundle admission and lineage use K. The three production strict callers omit O. The scalar `as_known` now also admits at K. Report reason codes shift slightly for O>K derived cells (`derived_operand_selection_changed` maps to `canonical_resolution_unavailable`).
Blocking: undisclosed discovery admission tightening (see blocking_findings).

Discovery and report no longer swallow ValueError/RuntimeError. Stored-value decode outside the typed boundaries, such as `date.fromisoformat(str(period_end)[:10])` and `GrowthFactReference.model_validate`, now aborts the screen instead of degrading. This misclassifies malformed stored cells as programmer failures.

Discovery now keeps corrupt cells local instead of failing the whole history. That is an intended policy change for tamper response, but older corrupt periods outside the 9-quarter window no longer degrade the result.
The scope cache lost its 4096-entry bound, so it is bounded only by operation lifetime. Cached `PublicationVerificationError` instances are re-raised repeatedly, which grows their traceback.
units.scope: Canonical ordered financial reads and one bounded recursive publication-verification cache

findings: Real retirement: parse, filter, cache, anchor and verdict reads moved out of workspace_data and the renderer. The renderer consumes prepared rows and indices only, and the purity test forbids parser, filter, cache, DB and file IO.

Preservation: all parsed rows are retained and selection is stored as indices into the full population. The cache key, store and invalidation are unchanged. Non-strict valid-subset and no-valid-id caching match the baseline. Strict dirty refresh validates before writing and fails on no parsable rows. Ordinary forced builds reuse the cache (one filter call across two builds).
Verdict availability mapping (missing table or read error means unavailable, empty result means empty) matches the baseline source.

Anchor-composition failure now falls back instead of crashing render. `llm_filtered` now reflects the actual model/cache disposition, so fallback-case HTML differs from the baseline. That is truthful, but not covered by the non-LLM golden.
units.scope: Prepared Say/Do section only (generated Markdown and other panel DB reads retained)
